answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake that decays only after a long history of verified useful work, so a new identity starts with a thin thread of trust. Every completed task sends a small pulse of reputation through the agent's record, and peers check that pulse before delegating valuable work. A Sybil attacker must fund and age thousands of separate stakes, while one bad act burns the stake and sends a ripple of distrust to linked accounts, making mass fake identities far more expensive than the rewards they could steal.
